thread:
sophie: Customer reported a sudden spike in 401s after upgrading our Go SDK to v2.0.0. They said nothing else changed on their side, just `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0` and their CI started failing. Repro steps below.
sophie: Repro (condensed):
1) clean GOPATH, `go mod tidy`
2) import `github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2` in code
3) build and run calls, get `401 unauthorized` from API. Logs show request reaches API but missing Authorization header.

kevin: Assigning myself. This smells like a module path/tag mismatch. Common mistake: tagged release v2 without module path `/v2` bump. Can you paste their `go.mod` and the module line from the tagged commit?

sophie: Customer pasted their `go.mod` snippet and output from `go list -m -mod=mod all`:
```
module example.com/repro

require (
  github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0
)
```
and `go list -m -json github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` shows `Path: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` (no "/v2" suffix) but version v2.0.0.

apoorv: Yep that's the root cause. If the repository published v2 tag but didn't update the `module` line to `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`, `go` will perform a pseudo-version rewrite that can cause the package to be fetched under the v1 path and break import resolution. That can lead to mismatched compiled code where middleware expectations (like attaching Authorization) differ.

marta: Quick workaround for customers: add a `replace` directive pointing to the commit that matches the v2 module path, or pin to our patched tag once we cut it. Example replace they can put in their `go.mod`:
```
replace github.com-redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 => github.com-redwood-inference/go-sdk v0.0.0-20240315000000-abcdef123456
```
Then `go mod tidy` and rebuild. Not ideal but unblocks CI. :+1: 

kevin: I'm going to validate the repo tags now. deploy-bot: show last release job for go-sdk.
deploy-bot: release job: `go-sdk` tag `v2.0.0` created by `ci-release` at 2024-05-21T12:03:22Z, commit `abcdef123456`. Module line in that commit: `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` (no /v2).

sophie: Ugh. So the publish pipeline created a v2 tag without updating module path. Customer impact: imports expecting `/v2` path (typical for Go) will get inconsistent semantics.

apoorv: Action plan: 1) Publish a patch tag `v2.0.1` with module path updated to `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2` and confirm `go list -m -json` shows Path with `/v2`. 2) Post a very short mitigation note to affected customers: add replace directive or pin to commit as marta suggested. 3) Add CI check to assure `module` path matches major tag.

kevin: I'll cut `v2.0.1` now. Also we should check if our header middleware changed package import path which could be why the Authorization header disappeared in some combinations. But likely it's the module mismatch causing two copies of middleware in the binary. When the same package appears with two module paths, types don't unify and runtime wiring can fail silently.

marta: Logging note to support: include `go env`, `go list -m -json github.com-redwood-inference/go-sdk`, and `grep module go.sum` when customers hit this. That helps triage quickly.

sophie: Customer unblocked with replace workaround, they're waiting for patched release. I'll notify them when `v2.0.1` is out.

kevin: Patch pushed, tag `v2.0.1` created, CI release started. Will announce once published. Also adding a postmortem entry to prevent repeat.

marta: Added follow-up checklist in our release playbook repo: require module version parity check and a `go test` verify step that imports `github.com-redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`.

sophie: Thanks all. I'll update the customer thread and close the escalation after confirmation. :pray:
